components.css: .ds-stub{--tear:62%;--notch:11px;position:relative;background:var(--stock,#ffd12e);color:#1a1814;border-radius:6px;padding:18px 20px;max-width:340px;font-family:var(--font-ui);-webkit-mask:radial-gradient(circle var(--notch) at 0 var(--tear),transparent 98%,#000 100%),radial-gradient(circle var(--notch) at 100% var(--tear),transparent 98%,#000 100%);-webkit-mask-composite:source-in;mask:radial-gradient(circle var(--notch) at 0 var(--tear),transparent 98%,#000 100%) intersect,radial-gradient(circle var(--notch) at 100% var(--tear),transparent 98%,#000 100%);filter:drop-shadow(0 6px 14px rgba(26,24,20,0.14));animation:ds-tear 280ms cubic-bezier(0.23,1,0.32,1) both}.ds-stub::after{content:'';position:absolute;left:15px;right:15px;top:var(--tear);border-top:2px dashed rgba(26,24,20,0.28)}.ds-stub-label{font-size:13px;font-weight:700;opacity:0.72}.ds-serial{font:800 88px/0.9 var(--font-num);letter-spacing:0.01em;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;margin:8px 0 14px}.ds-punches{display:flex;gap:7px;align-items:center;margin-bottom:28px}.ds-punches i{width:14px;height:14px;border-radius:50%;border:2px solid rgba(26,24,20,0.55)}.ds-punches i.d{background:#1a1814;border-color:#1a1814}.ds-punches i.y{width:18px;height:18px;border:3px solid #1a1814;box-shadow:0 0 0 3px rgba(255,255,255,0.6)}.ds-stub-foot{font-weight:650}@keyframes ds-tear{from{clip-path:inset(0 0 100% 0);transform:translateY(-6px)}to{clip-path:inset(0);transform:none}}@media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.ds-stub{animation-duration:1ms}}

narrative.overview:
Every promise Beautifood makes is a ticket you can hold. Queue numbers, preorders, open bills, kitchen tickets, bookings and branch summaries are drawn as stubs: a block of ticket stock, a stamped serial numeral in a tall condensed face, a dashed tear line, and on the full stub, half-moon perforation notches and a row of punched holes. The shell around them is a kopitiam-sign yellow bar with carbon ink, loud and local like good hawker-centre signage.

The stub is the one signature move. Everything else is a calm, standard working screen: white ground (warm charcoal in dark mode), hairline warm-grey rules, soft-shadowed cards, ink-filled primary buttons. Guest screens are one-handed and glanceable (the number always wins the viewport). Staff screens are dense but calm, with big tablet targets and state carried by a small, fixed set of tones. The system is fully bilingual (English and Simplified Chinese) and every layout holds for CJK text.

It rejects two things, both named in the direction contract: the category default (grey cards with one accent colour) and the gimmick (a fake paper-ticket skin over everything).
keyCharacteristics: Yellow shell bar, carbon ink, white or charcoal ground.
Ticket stock colour per party-size class: A yellow, B rose, C mint, D lilac, X neutral.
Serial numerals in Big Shoulders Display, tabular, stamped; everything else in Figtree with system CJK fallback.
Dashed tear lines separate a stub's serial from its body, at every scale.
Lucide icons at their default 2px stroke inline (15 to 19px), 1.75 beside section titles, 1.5 for large empty-state icons.
Short, decisive motion on a custom ease-out; reduced motion keeps only colour and opacity changes.

rules.name: The Ink-On-Yellow Rule
rules.body: Yellow is a fill, never a text colour on white. Text on yellow or on any stock is carbon (#1a1814), and stays carbon in dark mode.

rules.name: The Stock Means Class Rule
rules.body: Stock colours carry exactly one meaning: the party-size class letter of a ticket (A, B, C, D, else X). Never use rose, mint or lilac for decoration, charts or state.

rules.name: The Inverted Selection Rule
rules.body: Selected, pressed and active controls (nav tab, chip, language toggle, segmented POS bill, aria-pressed buttons) invert to a carbon fill with yellow text in light mode, and to a yellow fill with carbon text in dark mode.

rules.name: The Serial Face Rule
rules.body: Big Shoulders Display sets numbers, codes and short proper names on stubs (ticket numbers, table labels, prices, totals, branch names, the wordmark). It never sets sentences or headings.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Wherever figures sit (serials, money, stats, table cells, bill lines, chart labels) they are tabular, so columns and live-updating counts do not jitter.

rules.name: The CJK Breathing Rule
rules.body: For Chinese, heading tracking returns to 0 and body line-height opens to 1.65. Never apply negative or positive tracking to CJK text, and never rely on uppercase for emphasis: Chinese has none.

rules.name: The Number First Rule
rules.body: On guest screens the stub with the number and "what happens next" is the first thing in the viewport; actions stack below it as full-width big buttons.

rules.name: The Only Stubs Float Rule
rules.body: Drop-shadow filters belong to stubs. Every other surface uses the card ambient shadow or none.

rules.name: The Tear Line Rule
rules.body: A dashed carbon rule always separates the stock-coloured serial area of a stub from its content. Dashed borders elsewhere mean "not solid": blocked or split tables, QR cut sheets, the promo form divider.

rules.name: The Short Hands Rule
rules.body: Interaction motion stays under 300ms and moves only transform and opacity. The phone sheet (320ms), the lit-row wash fade (600ms) and meter fills (400ms) are the only longer transitions.

dos: **Do** draw any new numbered promise (ticket, bill, booking, order) as a stub: stock fill, serial face, dashed tear (The Tear Line Rule).
**Do** pick stub stock from the class letter of the number (A, B, C, D) and fall back to X for anything else or for a cancelled ticket.
**Do** put carbon (#1a1814) text on yellow and on every stock, in both colour schemes (The Ink-On-Yellow Rule).
**Do** set every figure tabular and set serials, prices and table labels in Big Shoulders Display.
**Do** write labels in sentence case and translate every string; check each new layout in Simplified Chinese at 1.65 line-height with zero tracking.
**Do** use Lucide icons: default stroke at 15 to 19px inline, 1.75 stroke beside section titles, 28 to 32px at 1.5 stroke in empty states.
**Do** keep tap targets at 42px or more (48px for kitchen bumps, 54px for guest primaries) and gate hover styles behind fine pointers.
**Do** honour prefers-reduced-motion and prefers-color-scheme for every new component.
donts: **Don't** use yellow as text on white or light surfaces.
**Don't** use rose, mint or lilac for anything except party-size class (The Stock Means Class Rule).
**Don't** add uppercase, letter-spaced kicker or eyebrow labels above headings or numbers; the stub's field labels are sentence case, and Chinese has no case to fall back on.
**Don't** turn whole screens into paper tickets; working screens stay standard and the stub is the one signature move.
**Don't** put a drop shadow on anything that is not a stub, or animate layout properties for interaction feedback.
**Don't** set sentences or headings in Big Shoulders Display, or apply negative tracking to CJK text.
**Don't** use emoji or text glyphs as icons; icons are Lucide or the stub wordmark.
